readmeHtml:
Run from the repository root (the directory containing labs). After downloading the archive, extract it and run from the extracted root.

sh
cd labs/go
go test -race ./gateway

Go requires 1.24 or newer. Python requires 3.11 or newer. The two LLM labs additionally require CPU-capable PyTorch in labs/.venv; see the collection instructions.

Tests use deterministic substitutes or synthetic tensors. No paid API, cloud service, model-weight download, GPU, or external project checkout is required. A failed test is a correctness issue to investigate; raw timing changes alone do not fail the tests.

Read the source and tests together. The article's code excerpts are extracted from marked regions in these files during the website build.

// Package gateway is a teaching admission gate inspired by go-review's gateway.
package gateway

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"sync"
)

var ErrCapacity = errors.New("capacity exhausted")
var ErrDraining = errors.New("gate is draining")

type Gate struct {
	mu            sync.Mutex
	limit, active int
	draining      bool
	done          chan struct{}
}

func New(limit int) (*Gate, error) {
	if limit < 1 {
		return nil, errors.New("limit must be positive")
	}
	return &Gate{limit: limit, done: make(chan struct{})}, nil
}

// Start acquires capacity before creating work. The caller owns cancellation.
// region:admission
func (g *Gate) Start(ctx context.Context, work func(context.Context) error) (<-chan error, error) {
	if work == nil {
		return nil, errors.New("nil work")
	}
	g.mu.Lock()
	defer g.mu.Unlock()
	if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	if g.draining {
		return nil, ErrDraining
	}
	if g.active == g.limit {
		return nil, ErrCapacity
	}
	g.active++
	result := make(chan error, 1)
	go func() {
		defer func() {
			g.mu.Lock()
			g.active--
			if g.draining && g.active == 0 {
				close(g.done)
			}
			g.mu.Unlock()
			close(result)
		}()
		result <- work(ctx)
	}()
	return result, nil
}

// endregion:admission

// Shutdown stops admission and waits for workers. A timeout does not kill work.
// region:shutdown
func (g *Gate) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) error {
	g.mu.Lock()
	if !g.draining {
		g.draining = true
		if g.active == 0 {
			close(g.done)
		}
	}
	g.mu.Unlock()
	select {
	case <-g.done:
		return nil
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	}
}

// endregion:shutdown

func (g *Gate) Active() int { g.mu.Lock(); defer g.mu.Unlock(); return g.active }

package gateway

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func deadline(t *testing.T) context.Context {
	t.Helper()
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
	t.Cleanup(cancel)
	return ctx
}
func result(t *testing.T, ctx context.Context, ch <-chan error) error {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case err := <-ch:
		return err
	case <-ctx.Done():
		t.Fatal("worker did not finish")
		return ctx.Err()
	}
}
func TestCapacityAndDrain(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := deadline(t)
	g, _ := New(2)
	release := make(chan struct{})
	started := make(chan struct{}, 2)
	work := func(ctx context.Context) error {
		started <- struct{}{}
		select {
		case <-release:
			return nil
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return ctx.Err()
		}
	}
	first, _ := g.Start(ctx, work)
	second, _ := g.Start(ctx, work)
	<-started
	<-started
	if g.Active() != 2 {
		t.Fatal("wrong active count")
	}
	if _, err := g.Start(ctx, work); !errors.Is(err, ErrCapacity) {
		t.Fatalf("wanted capacity error: %v", err)
	}
	expired, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
	cancel()
	if err := g.Shutdown(expired); !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		t.Fatalf("shutdown must wait: %v", err)
	}
	if _, err := g.Start(ctx, work); !errors.Is(err, ErrDraining) {
		t.Fatalf("wanted draining: %v", err)
	}
	close(release)
	if err := result(t, ctx, first); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := result(t, ctx, second); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := g.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := g.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if g.Active() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("capacity leaked")
	}
}
func TestCancellationAndErrorRelease(t *testing.T) {
	for _, mode := range []string{"cancel", "failure"} {
		t.Run(mode, func(t *testing.T) {
			ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(deadline(t))
			defer cancel()
			g, _ := New(1)
			ch, err := g.Start(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
				if mode == "failure" {
					return errors.New("upstream failure")
				}
				<-ctx.Done()
				return ctx.Err()
			})
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if mode == "cancel" {
				cancel()
			}
			if result(t, deadline(t), ch) == nil {
				t.Fatal("missing work error")
			}
			if err := g.Shutdown(deadline(t)); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if g.Active() != 0 {
				t.Fatal("slot leak")
			}
		})
	}
}
func TestConcurrentAdmissionAndShutdown(t *testing.T) {
	ctx := deadline(t)
	g, _ := New(3)
	var callers sync.WaitGroup
	for range 100 {
		callers.Add(1)
		go func() {
			defer callers.Done()
			ch, err := g.Start(ctx, func(context.Context) error { return nil })
			if err == nil {
				<-ch
			} else if !errors.Is(err, ErrCapacity) && !errors.Is(err, ErrDraining) {
				t.Errorf("unexpected error %v", err)
			}
		}()
	}
	if err := g.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	callers.Wait()
	if g.Active() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("work survived shutdown")
	}
}
func TestInvalidInputs(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := New(0); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("zero limit accepted")
	}
	g, _ := New(1)
	if _, err := g.Start(context.Background(), nil); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("nil worker accepted")
	}
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	cancel()
	if _, err := g.Start(ctx, func(context.Context) error { return nil }); !errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
}
